senses.gloss: m. (סָרַק I) barrenness, desert.—אילן ס׳ a tree which bears no fruit; shade-tree, wild-tree.
units: Kil. VI, 5 (ref. to ib. 3) איזהו אילן ס׳ כל שאינו וכ׳ what tree is meant by illan s’raḳ? Any tree which bears no fruit; (oth. opin.) הכל א׳ ס׳ חוץ מן הזית וכ׳ all trees are s’raḳ, except olive and fig trees; (oth. opin.) כל שאין … הרי זה א׳ ס׳ whatever trees you do not plant in orchards, are called illan s’raḳ.

<cite ref="Bava Kamma 91b:21">B. Kam. 91ᵇ</cite> (ref. to <cite ref="Deuteronomy 20:20">Deut. XX, 20</cite>) <he>כי לא עץ … זה א׳ ס׳</he> ‘that it is not a fruit tree’, that means a tree which bears no edible fruit; <he>להקדים ס׳ למאכל</he> (sub. <he>אילן</he>) to prefer (for cutting down) the barren tree to one that has edible fruit; <cite ref="Sifrei Devarim 204:2">Sifré Deut. 204</cite>.

<cite ref="Bereishit Rabbah 16:3">Gen. R. s. 16</cite> <he>אומרים לאילני ס׳ וכ׳</he> they ask the fruitless trees, why are you so noisy? <cite ref="Bereishit Rabbah 16:3">Ib.</cite> <he>אבל אילני ס׳ וכ׳</he> but the shade-trees are loud, because they are not burdened with fruit; a. fr.
